ileal: Of or pertaining to the ileum.
ileum: The last, and usually the longest, division of the small intestine; the part between the jejunum and large intestine.
ileus: Disruption of the normal propulsive ability of the gastrointestinal tract, due to failure of peristalsis.
iliad: An Ancient Greek epic poem, ascribed to Homer, which depicts events near the end of the Trojan War.
ilial: Archaic form of iliac (“Pertaining to the ilium”).
ilium: The upper and widest of the three bones that make up each side of the hipbone.
illation: The act of inferring or concluding, especially from a set of premises; a conclusion, a deduction.
illative: Of, or relating to an illation.
illaudably: In a way that is not laudable, or praiseworthy.
illegal: Contrary to, forbidden, or not authorized by law, especially criminal law.
illegalization: The act or process of illegalizing.
illegalize: To make illegal; to prohibit by law, to criminalize.
illegalized: simple past and past participle of illegalize
illegalizes: third-person singular simple present indicative of illegalize
illegalizing: present participle and gerund of illegalize
illegally: In a manner contrary to law.
illegibility: The characteristic or quality of being illegible; the quality of being difficult or impossible to read.
illegible: Not clear enough to be read; unreadable; not legible or decipherable.
illegibly: In a manner that produces illegible results.
illegitimate: Not conforming to known principles, or established or accepted rules or standards.
iller: comparative form of ill: more ill
illest: superlative form of ill: most ill
illiberal: Restricting or failing to sufficiently promote individual choice and freedom.
illiberalism: The principle, state or quality of being illiberal.
illiberalness: The state of being illiberal; illiberality.
illicit: Not approved by law, but not invalid.
illicitly: In an illicit manner; illegally, immorally, or inappropriately.
illimitableness: The quality of being illimitable; absence of limits.
illiquidity: The condition of being illiquid; a lack of liquidity; difficulty in selling out an asset.
illite: A micaceous phyllosilicate clay mineral with aggregates of grey or white monoclinic crystals.
illiteracy: The inability to read and write.
illitic: Of or relating to the mineral illite.
illness: An instance (episode) of a disease or poor health.
illocutionary: Of, pertaining to, or deriving from illocution, the performance of acts by speaking.
illogical: Contrary to logic; lacking sense or sound reasoning.
illogically: In an illogical manner, without following methods of sane and correct reasoning, in a manner lacking thought or logic.
illume: To throw or spread light upon; to make light or bright.
illumed: simple past and past participle of illume
illumes: third-person singular simple present indicative of illume
illuminable: that can be illuminated or made lighter
illuminance: The luminous flux incident on unit area of a surface; commonly measured in lux (lumen/metre²) or otherwise foot-candles.
illumination: The act of illuminating, or supplying with light; the state of being illuminated.
illuminative: of, capable of, or causing illumination
illumines: third-person singular simple present indicative of illumine
illuming: present participle and gerund of illume
illumining: present participle and gerund of illumine
illuminist: Someone who subscribes to the doctrine of illuminism, or who claims to have achieved spiritual illumination; one of the Illuminati.
illusion: A distortion of sensory perception where real stimuli lead to a false or misleading impression of reality.
illusional: Illusory; being or pertaining to an illusion.
illusionary: Illusory; pertaining to an illusion, or of the nature of an illusion.
illusionist: One who works with illusion or sleight of hand.
illusive: Subject to or pertaining to an illusion, often used in the sense of an unrealistic expectation or an unreachable goal or outcome.
illusory: Resulting from an illusion; deceptive, imaginary, unreal.
illustrate: To clarify something by giving, or serving as, an example or a comparison.
illustrated: simple past and past participle of illustrate
illustrates: third-person singular simple present indicative of illustrate
illustrating: present participle and gerund of illustrate
illustration: The act of illustrating; the act of making clear and distinct.
illustrative: Demonstrative, exemplative, showing an example or demonstrating.
illustrator: a person who draws pictures (especially illustrations in books or magazines)
illuvial: Of, pertaining to, or formed by illuviation
illuviated: simple past and past participle of illuviate
illuviation: The accumulation of suspended material and soluble compounds leached from an overlying stratum
illuvium: material displaced across a soil profile, from one layer to another, by the action of rainwater
ilmenite: A weakly magnetic dark gray mineral found in metamorphic and igneous rocks; it is a mixed oxide of iron and titanium, FeTiO₃
